name: Isolated Optic Nerve Aplasia

criteria.description: Complete absence of the optic nerve on neuroimaging
Absence of optic disc on fundoscopic examination
No associated systemic or neurological malformations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent optic nerve on imaging and absent optic disc on fundoscopic exam without other systemic anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may be considered to exclude syndromic forms.

imaging: MRI demonstrating absence of optic nerve
Absence of optic nerve sheath complex on orbital imaging
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified in isolated cases
Genetic testing to exclude syndromic optic nerve aplasia
other: Visual evoked potentials absent or severely reduced

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of thin but present optic nerve
Reduced rather than absent visual evoked potentials
Optic nerve hypoplasia rather than aplasia
Midline brain abnormalities such as absence of septum pellucidum

redFlags: Sudden onset of visual loss (suggests acquired cause)
Presence of systemic malformations or neurological deficits
